reason: Researched via WebSearch/WebFetch (Trading Economics, Reuters wrap, Yahoo Finance, TSMC Q3 coverage, Finviz sector table through the 10-16 close). What happened: the PHLX chip index fell eight straight sessions (longest streak since 2008), Nasdaq -4.5% on the week, driven by AI-credit worries (CoreWeave bonds yielding >15%, Anthropic IPO valuation doubts, OpenAI revenue questions, Microsoft's Maia 300), a hot September CPI (3.7%) and PPI, and Brent surging to ~$110 on Iranian tanker strikes in Hormuz. The 10-year actually fell 14bp on the week to ~5.1% on flight-to-safety; the Fed (Warsh) is expected to hold on Oct 27-28 with a December hike ~77-92% priced. Why hold rather than trade: (1) the barbell did exactly what it was built for - the AI sleeve (NVDA -10.4%, AVGO -9.3%, ANET -14.5%) is inside its 18% stops while BRK-B +5.5%, XLE +7.6% (energy was the best sector on every horizon, +4.5% this week), MRK +4.6% and JNJ +1.0% carried the book, and NAV is +2.9% vs SPY +1.9% with a max drawdown of only -2.9%; (2) the fundamentals under the AI sleeve were reaffirmed this week, not refuted - TSMC posted record Q3 revenue (+50.9% y/y), guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B, said AI demand still exceeds its supply, and lifted capex to ~$64B; ASML said it cannot fully meet 2027-28 demand. The selloff is about the financing of second-tier AI builders and about rates, not about demand for NVDA/AVGO/ANET silicon; (3) selling 25% of the book into the longest chip losing streak in 18 years, with 40% cash already earning 4%, would be selling the low of a correction the book was designed to absorb, and the stops remain the pre-committed exit if the credit story spreads to the hyperscalers - ANET at -14.5% is the leg nearest its stop and if it goes it goes; (4) the catalysts that will resolve this (META capex commentary, TSLA and NFLX next week, MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN and the FOMC the week after) are days away, and repositioning in front of them at these prices adds churn without information. I considered rotating ANET into more XLE but chasing energy after +7.6% in two weeks on a Hormuz premium that the IEA is already trying to cap with a 100M-barrel release is its own risk. Risks accepted: the AI-credit contagion widens and the sleeve stops out (cost roughly 1-2% of NAV beyond current marks); JNJ's Q3 talc charge and soft MedTech are known and the stock has already recovered above my fill.
